title: France's debt crisis and high school protests draw global attention
subhead: French high school student protests have drawn major media coverage and political reactions in the US, Italy, Belgium and the UK. Only a few countries, such as Germany, wracked by its own domestic political debates, have treated the situation with restraint.

'Trump dividend': Can promising voters a check help win an election?
subhead: Donald Trump is promising $5,000 to every adult US citizen if both chambers remain Republican after the midterm elections on November 3. In his column, Le Monde's Pascal Riché recalls that Silvio Berlusconi and Emmanuel Macron also used financial incentives during their campaigns.

title: Paris officials seek to reduce the area under heritage protection in the capital
subhead: Paris' left-wing government plans to review the scope of what is considered a 'Remarkable Heritage Site,' which it deems too extensive. Currently, it includes the first seven arrondissements of the capital, as well as parts of four others.

title: Lutetia wall: 'An archeological discovery can be instantaneous, but knowledge never is'
subhead: Following the discovery of a Gallic wall at the Hôtel-Dieu hospital in Paris, archeologist William Van Andringa writes that we cannot make stones speak before we have truly questioned them.

title: The letter of imprisoned Russian journalist Ivan Safronov: 'Like Jean Valjean, I know what captivity is, and I know how to cherish freedom'
subhead: Safronov, a prisoner of conscience who was arrested in 2020 and is now detained in Siberia, turns to literature as a lifeline. He recently reread Victor Hugo's Les Misérables. Here is the letter he sent to Le Monde about this classic.

subhead: Increasingly criticized after footage emerged showing heavy-handed police tactics and injured teenagers, Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez is not toning down his communication. Law enforcement says 6,059 arrests were made between September 28 and October 5, a record number.

title: French high school protests: 'Young people are not fooled by the discrimination and contempt that society directs at them'
subhead: Sociologist and child psychiatrist Laelia Benoit analyzes the discourse surrounding high school student protests through the lens of 'childism,' a term that refers to the set of prejudices against minors based on their age, which she introduced to France.

title: What students are saying during high school blockades: 'I am worried about my future and for all students in France'
